subject: Business
title: Decision Fatigue in Organizations
description: A 60-second lesson on Decision Fatigue in Organizations.

hook.text: Judges grant parole at 65% in the morning and near 0% before lunch. Tired brains default to 'no.'

buildup.text: Decision fatigue means the quality of decisions deteriorates after making many in a row.

discovery.text: Organizations that require too many approvals exhaust decision-makers. Quality drops; speed disappears.

twist.text: Steve Jobs wore the same outfit daily to eliminate one decision. Bezos makes key decisions before 10 AM.

climax.text: The fix: reduce decision volume through policies, defaults, and delegation. Save energy for what matters.

punchline.text: Every small decision uses the same fuel as a big one.

quiz.question: How can organizations reduce decision fatigue?
options: Use defaults, policies, and delegation to reduce decision volume
Require every team member to approve every decision
Schedule all important meetings in the evening

details.summary: Decision fatigue is the deterioration of decision quality after making many consecutive decisions. In organizations, it leads to poor strategic choices made late in long meetings, approval of default options, and avoidance of difficult decisions by exhausted leaders.
details.whyItMatters: Organizations make hundreds of decisions daily. When leaders are depleted from trivial choices, they make worse high-stakes decisions. Structuring decision processes to conserve cognitive energy directly improves strategic outcomes.
takeaways: Decision quality deteriorates measurably after extended decision-making sessions
Depleted decision-makers default to the status quo or the easiest option
Scheduling important decisions early and reducing trivial ones improves outcomes

faq.question: How does decision fatigue affect business outcomes?
faq.answer: Studies of judges show parole approval drops from 65% to nearly zero before lunch breaks and recovers afterward. In business, executives making budget decisions late in the day approve status quo budgets rather than evaluating changes. Important decisions get poor attention.

faq.question: What can organizations do to reduce decision fatigue?
faq.answer: Schedule high-stakes decisions for morning when cognitive resources are fresh. Eliminate trivial decisions through policies and defaults. Break long decision sessions with breaks. Delegate low-stakes decisions downward. Limit meeting agendas to essential decisions only.
